questions.q: What is a balanced diet, and what are the main components of food?
answer: A balanced diet is one that contains all the nutrients the body needs, in the right amounts, along with roughage and water.

answer.text: Food provides carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals. Carbohydrates and fats give energy; proteins build and repair the body; vitamins and minerals protect it from disease.
Dietary fibre, or roughage, is not digested but helps remove waste, while water aids digestion and controls body temperature.
Eating the right amount — neither too much nor too little — keeps the body healthy; over-eating leads to obesity.

questions.q: List the main deficiency diseases and the nutrients whose lack causes them.
answer: When the diet lacks a particular nutrient for a long time, a deficiency disease results.

answer.text: Lack of Vitamin A causes night blindness; Vitamin B1, beriberi; Vitamin C, scurvy (bleeding gums); and Vitamin D, rickets (weak, bent bones).
Lack of iron causes anaemia, lack of iodine causes goitre, and lack of calcium leads to weak bones and teeth.
These diseases can be prevented by eating a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, pulses, milk and, where needed, iodised salt.

questions.q: Describe the simple tests used to detect starch, protein and fat in food.
answer: Simple chemical tests reveal which nutrients a food contains.

answer.text: A few drops of iodine solution are added to the food. If starch is present, the food turns blue-black.
A solution of copper sulphate and caustic soda is added to the food. If protein is present, a violet colour appears.
The food item is rubbed on a piece of paper. If fat is present, it leaves a translucent, oily (grease) spot that lets light through.

answer: These tests let us check the main components of everyday foods.
